data.name: Fazli
data.gender_notes: Fazli is used as a male name in Islamic naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: Derived from the Arabic word 'fazlah' which means prosperity, success, and abundance. In the Quran, the term 'fazl' is used to describe the blessings and favor of Allah upon His servants. The name Fazli carries the meaning “Successful, Prosperous” and is chosen by families in Islamic traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Arabic tradition and is also used in Arabic, Urdu, Persian. Parents who choose Fazli usually hope their child will grow to embody successful, prosperous and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: Symbolizes the blessings and favor of Allah in one's life.
data.etymology: Fazli belongs to the Arabic linguistic tradition and is used in Islamic naming. Its recorded meaning is “Successful, Prosperous.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Fazli total 9, giving a life-path number of 9. Number 9 is linked with Mars and with the qualities of compassion, idealism and generosity.

data.cultural_impact: The name Fazli holds a significant cultural impact as it is a source of inspiration and pride for many parents who wish to bless their children with the blessings of abundance, prosperity, and success. The name is well-received and cherished in the Islamic community as it reflects the belief in the power of Allah's blessings and the importance of striving for success in life.
data.spiritual_significance: From a spiritual perspective, the name Fazli is a constant reminder of the belief in the generous blessings of Allah. It serves as a source of motivation and inspiration for the individual to strive towards success and prosperity in this world while keeping their faith in Allah as the ultimate source of all good things. It also reflects the belief that all success and prosperity ultimately come from Allah and serve as a means to please Him and serve His creation. Ultimately, the name Fazli embodies the Islamic principle of Tawakkul (total reliance on Allah) and the belief that all success and prosperity come from Allah's Mercy and Favor (Fazl).
